facts.text: Clitherall’s first permanent settlement began in 1865 when a group of Cutlerite Latter‑Day Saints from Iowa established a colony on the north shore of Clitherall Lake.
The colony, originally led by Alpheus Cutler, later passed leadership to Chauncey Whiting after Cutler’s death.
Clitherall was platted in October 1881 and named after Clitherall Lake, itself named for Major George B. — a former slaveowner and presidential appointee.
Local historians call the Clitherall Lake colony “the first and, in many ways, one of the most interesting” early Otter Tail settlement because of its distinct religious community.
The original settlement’s legacy lives on in regional museum collections and interpretive programs that document its migration and cooperative community.
A vanguard group of seven families, including the Whiting, Fletcher, and Tucker families, left Iowa in 1864, braving blizzards before settling on Clitherall Lake’s north shore.
